elements.quote: To be included in this review, studies had to explore facilitators and/or barriers to PA in older patients during hospitalization. Studies were included if: 1) they were published between January 1, 2000, and May 29, 2021; 2) they were written in English, German, or Dutch; 3) they used a quantitative, qualitative, or mixed-methods study design; and 4) the study population consisted of patients aged ≥ 65 years (baseline mean age of 65 years or older), caregivers, or HCPs.
elements.reason: Specifies study designs, settings, population, and time frame, but follow-up requirements are not mentioned.

elements.quote: studies were included if: 1) they were published between January 1, 2000, and May 29, 2021; 2) they were written in English, German, or Dutch; ... Studies were excluded if they were: 1) editorials, opinion papers, conference abstracts, or literature reviews; ...
elements.reason: Eligibility criteria for report characteristics including dissemination year, language, and publication status are specified.
The evidence does not indicate that exclusion was based on outcomes not measured versus not reported; such distinction is not made in the eligibility criteria.

elements.quote: The level of evidence of facilitators and/or barriers from quantitative studies and quantitative parts of mixedmethods studies was assessed using the best evidence synthesis approach [40, 41]. The approach was applied to facilitators and barriers that were reported at least once in RCTs or at least twice in non-randomized studies. ... Subsequently, the overall quality scores of each study were used to group studies into two categories: high (MMAT score 4 or 5) and low (MMAT score 0-3) quality.
elements.reason: Groups used in synthesis (based on study design and quality) are specified and linked to the evidence synthesis approach, which relates to the review's objective of identifying facilitators and barriers.

elements.quote: Given the specific hospital setting in the current review, in which patients enter a different and unfamiliar context, it is conceivable that facilitators and barriers might be different for patients over 65 years than for younger patients.
elements.reason: Rationale is provided for focusing on older patients and hospital setting, but not for other restrictions like language or publication year.
No evidence of the date when each information source was last searched is reported.

elements.quote:
Table 1 Best evidence synthesis guidelines

| Level of evidence   | Explanation                                                                                                                                                                              |
|---------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Strong              | Consistent ­ findings a in two or more RCTs of high quality (MMAT score 4 or 5).                                                                                                         |
| Moderate            | Consistent findings in one high-quality RCT and one or more RCTs of low quality (MMAT score 0-3), or one high-quality RCT and one or more high-quality non-rand- omized studies.         |
| Limited             | Consistent findings in one high-quality RCT, or two or more high-quality non-ran- domized studies, or one or more high-quality non-randomized studies, and one or more low-quality RCTs. |
| Conflicting         | contradictory findings, with less than 75% of the studies reporting consistent findings.                                                                                                 |
| Insufficient        | The above criteria were not met.                                                                                                                                                         |
